checked_decisions: Slot 20/21 speaker pairing (Gain Bijou 21020 briefing, Ruri Hoshino 12031 providing unmanned support ships): source data assigns these operator ids directly; per orchestrator decision speaker tags are never changed even when a pairing looks unusual. Kept as sourced.

Slot 21 'unmanned support ships' for mujin engokan: the source clause carries no <book()> reference to the Flail encyclopedia entry (book(6), locked in encyclopedia_021_a.json), so this is a distinct, unnamed asset rather than literally 'Flail'; the generic descriptive rendering is correct and does not conflict with 'drone unit' used for a different Japanese term (mujinki butai) in 4003631 - different source words, different generic renderings, consistent.

Slot 22 'are mostly wiped out' / 'the operation will fail' passive constructions verified to preserve source clause order (color(4) span before color(6) span) and causal logic (losing most of the unmanned ships -> front line falls -> operation fails).
'Invaders' (slot 0) and all faction/speaker names checked; no glossary conflicts.

All commands (<operator>, <speed>, <move>, <marker>, <picture>, <refer>, <danger>, <delpic>, <enemylist>) verified identical in count and order versus source for every row; ASCII-only, no newline, and 128-visible-char limit verified for every row; no bare % found.
remaining_uncertainties: Slot 20 'wipe out every target' omits the explicit enemy-no (敵の) modifier attached to the target in source; left as-is because 'target' unambiguously reads as an enemy target in this HUD-driven briefing convention (compare 4003641 'aim only for the targets', which also omits an explicit 'enemy' in its English despite context settling it), but flagged for awareness.
Slot 21 'unmanned support ships' has no project-wide locked term for mujin engokan; if a later glossary pass names this asset, align this row.

Slot 34-style cross-cast pairing (Gain Bijou + Ruri Hoshino) is unusual versus the rest of the reviewed corpus; kept as sourced per the never-change-speaker-tags rule, flagged for the orchestrator's awareness rather than as a translation defect.
